summary: Franklin County, ME tower on Bald Mountain in Rangeley; 1920s, replaced 1994; cab gone per FFLA; an August 2026 Sun Journal piece tells readers to climb the lookout.

facts.design: Metal lookout with an observation platform and no cab
facts.status_note: Still standing, but its cab is gone, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association

access.note: Trail is on state land and open to the public; an August 2026 newspaper piece tells readers to climb the lookout and warns they may have to wait their turn

visit.trail_note: Two trailheads, on Carry Road and Bald Mountain Road; one trail is 2.5 miles round trip and the other 3.9 miles, with rock scrambles near the top; condition not inspected

events.note: The 2021 Sun Journal list gives the tower as 1920s (replaced 1994); the replacement is not described further

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A hiking site describes a tower cab; the FFLA asterisk and the 2021 Sun Journal list say the cab is gone, and the 2026 Sun Journal describes a metal lookout with a top platform and no cab. The story follows the newspapers and FFLA, and says the cab claim is unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Identity: FFLA 'Oquossoc Bald' (44.94354, -70.77553) is treated as the Bald Mountain tower near Oquossoc, because the 2021 Sun Journal calls it 'Oquossoc Bald Mountain, Rangeley' and the 2026 piece calls it the 'Bald Mountain fire tower in Oquossoc'. Coordinates were not checked against a newspaper location. The built date is only '1920s' in the sources read, so no built event is recorded. OpenStreetMap node 7624268161 is tagged disused=yes (version 1, about six years old); not relied on. Preserve Pals says 'climbable and maintained' and 'one adult up at a time', but the same site says the author has not been there; not used. The brief's status_note is kept because the FFLA asterisk supports it. No recent inspection or staffing history found. Visit climbability rests on the 2026 newspaper; the condition is not independently confirmed, so the editor may want to flag it. Used 2 WebSearch and about 6 page reads.
